To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nonlinear optical properties of plasmonic hotspots are highly tunable and can be exploited for active control of multifrequency antennas.

we have demonstrated that a resonant pump field in a plasmonically enhanced hotspot mediates ultrafast optical nonlinear interactions between different antenna elements, and that we have experimentally isolated this nonlinear effect from slower thermal effects.
we have developed a method to transfer nonlinear interactions between elements of a plasmonic nanostructure, which allows for ultrafast nonlinear switching of multifrequency plamsonic antennas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of active plasmonic nanostructures for applications in nanophotonics.
ultrafast nonlinear control and manipulation of plasmonic hotspots.
the fundamental properties of plasmonic hotspots, with the ultimate goal of understanding the limits of plasmonic nonlinearities, and developing new applications for nonlinear plasmonic devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated that resonant pumping in a plasmon hotspot produces an efficient nonlinear transfer of optical Kerr effect to the readout antenna element.
the authors have shown that a nonlinear medium in the hot spot between two gold nanodisks can be used to transfer optical nonlinearity from one antenna to another.
this work shows that resonant pumping can be used to transfer optical nonlinearity between elements in a multifrequency plasmon antenna.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonlinear optical properties of the hotspot can be used as a tool for controlling the optical properties of the nanoantenna.
the Kerr nonlinearity can be transferred between different plasmonic nanostructures.

we have demonstrated that the nonlinear optical properties of a plasmonic nanostructure can be controlled by the excitation conditions of the nanostructure itself, rather than the external optical excitation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kerr nonlinearity can be transferred between antenna elements by resonantly exciting a nonlinear hotspot.
the nonlinear optical properties of a plasmonic antenna can be controlled in a spatially and specturally selective manner by using a nonlinear medium as a mediator.
the nonlinear optical properties of a plasmonic antenna can be precisely tuned by the optical field in a hotspot.
